# iothub_module_twin (Resource)

Manages part of a module twin: the tags and desired properties you declare. Reported properties are read-only, in the `iothub_module_twin` data source.

## Ownership

The twin belongs to the module. This resource does not create or delete it. It manages only the innermost keys declared in `tags` and `desired_properties`, leaving other keys untouched. This allows independent resources and systems to share a twin, but writers that manage the same key overwrite one another, including `iothub_configuration` and `iothub_scheduled_job` twin patches.

Omitting a previously managed key removes it from the twin. Destroying the resource removes all of its managed keys. Arrays and empty objects are single values. Omit a key instead of setting it to `null`. After import, the first apply adopts the declared keys without deleting any others.

Keys and values must follow the [twin format rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/iot-hub/iot-hub-devguide-device-twins#tags-and-properties-format). JSON formatting, object key order and `2` versus `2.0` do not cause drift.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "iothub_module" "telemetry" {
  device_id = "sensor-0001"
  module_id = "telemetry"
}

# Manages exactly desired.interval and desired.sinks. The rest is left alone.
resource "iothub_module_twin" "telemetry" {
  device_id = iothub_module.telemetry.device_id
  module_id = iothub_module.telemetry.module_id

  desired_properties = jsonencode({
    interval = 30
    sinks    = ["hub", "local"]
  })
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `device_id` (String) ID of the device the module belongs to. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `module_id` (String) Module ID. Changing it replaces the resource.

### Optional

- `desired_properties` (String) The desired properties to manage, as a JSON object (`jsonencode`).
- `tags` (String) The tags to manage, as a JSON object (`jsonencode`).

### Read-Only

- `etag` (String) ETag of the twin.
- `id` (String) `<device_id>/<module_id>`. Also the import ID. Every twin resource that manages the same twin has the same `id`.
- `version` (Number) Version of the twin.

## Import

```shell
# Import ID: <device_id>/<module_id>
terraform import iothub_module_twin.telemetry sensor-0001/telemetry
```
